rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly with no ICE fallback, so this candidate shifts from a conservative baseline toward stronger obfuscation while respecting the program's profile: a small (8.8 KB text, 41 functions) ray-tracing-style benchmark with a few compute-heavy hot functions (CalcObject, CalcObjectChildren, RotateMatrix) plus trig code, meaning control-flow-heavy passes must stay selective to keep runtime acceptable. SUB and SPLIT are cheap, low-risk transformations and get high cost-dimension weights so they apply broadly across all 41 functions, seeding diversity cheaply. BCF and FLA get raised SecurityGain weights (0.8) to intensify control-flow confusion on the larger functions that dominate the reverse-engineering surface, but their RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights are kept moderate (0.6) so the selector still steers them away from hot trig/geometry loops where bogus edges and flattening dispatch would hurt most. IBR and ICALL provide indirection that compounds with flattening (breaking static CFG recovery and call-graph analysis) and are given solid security weight with tolerance for their call-time overhead on non-critical paths. IGV stays the weakest signal: on a small single-module program its global-variable indirection adds little analytical resistance relative to its correctness and layout risk, so it remains a low-priority filler. Overall the table trades a modest, bounded runtime/size budget for substantially higher security and diversity than the round-1 baseline, with CorrectnessRisk weights retaining enough selectivity to avoid applying risky combinations to fragile functions.
